column1: # Band units (UnitType: GDAL_METADATA or the .aux.xml side file) and the class Raven gives them (GWGeoTIFF::BandUnit,
# src/GWGeoTIFF.cpp). The rule is closed: the raster is read as metres only when the whole text, normalised, is a metre form:
# a metre word, symbol or abbreviation, alone or followed by a listed vertical datum ("m MSL", "m (NAVD88)", "mAHD", "m above
# sea level"), a metre form in brackets after a metre word ("meter (m)") or after a quantity ("elevation (m)", "height in
#   M read as metres;  N no unit (read as metres);
#   S the run stops with a message naming the text and the remedy (METRES after the file name);
#   F the run stops: another length unit and no metre, or another length named with its metre conversion ("its elevations
#     are in ..."); METRES does not lift it;
#   X the run stops: a scaled metre (a part or multiple, a number with a factor sign or word, or a number and a metre as
#     the whole text); METRES does not lift it.
# METRES after the file name states that the values are metres for a text of class S (and N and M): such a raster is read as
# metres, and Raven writes a warning naming the file's own unit; F and X stop also with METRES. A dotted abbreviation may lack
# its final dot, "above" may precede a datum, and a blank may precede a datum's year ("m a.s.l", "m above MSL", "m (RH 2000)").
# Normalising: full-width characters as ASCII, no-break and ideographic spaces as blanks, blanks trimmed and runs of them as
# one, lower case (Greek without its accents), and surrounding brackets removed ("()" and "[]" alone are a text, class S).
# Read by geotiff_check.py; columns: class, a TAB, the text.
# -- other texts (METRES reads them as metres)
